bearing_on_the_pending_decisions.event_window_wording: Whether a Part III purpose sentence that continues with a subordinate clause, in a note the markup splits into more blocks, is the approved class. Accepting it is a revision of the approved wording, so it is set out here and not made in code.
bearing_on_the_pending_decisions.statement_values: The conditional rule finding.json recommends (a no-new-financial-statements declaration present and no native facts outside the governance taxonomy) holds on this amendment too. That is a second positive; there is still no negative example in this corpus, so the objection recorded there is narrowed, not answered.

consequence_today: The classifier cannot classify it, and the policy clears only what it classifies. So at FY2024 the event window is not cleared either - the six event metrics are refused by name (HISTORICAL_AMENDMENT_INPUT_CLASS_NOT_CLEARED:FISCAL_EVENT_WINDOW:UNCLASSIFIED(...)) where the successor's amendment clears them. Statement values would not have been cleared under either wording, so that part of the cost is the pending statement decision, not this.
how_it_came_up: Reading the predecessor's FY2024 into the historical frame (Issue #47 section 7.3) put a second Part III amendment in front of the approved classifier. finding.json beside this file reviewed the first and recorded, as the case against its own recommendation, that the recommended condition had been checked on one positive and no negative.
